newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Wednesday with early-maturing contracts rising due to the continued bull run on the domestic A share market, traders said.
But late-maturing contracts fell on market uncertainty after Beijing announced last Friday the establishment of a national state debt depository, they said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 9.98 percent from 9.51 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market plunged to 2.9 million lots from 5.7 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said continued rises on the Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets on Wednesday supported the early-maturing contracts with institutions borrowing to trade in stocks.

But institutions were reluctant to borrow later-maturing contracts due to fears the depository will take over the settlement of state debt transactions from all the regional markets, casting uncertainty over the Shanghai market's role, they said.
The trend of shorter-term contracts strengthening and longer-term contracts weakening is likely to continue for a while, traders said.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Wednesday thanks to their favorable yields. But trading continued to be dull with liquidity flowing out to the more active stock markets, traders said.
The most actively traded three-year bond, which matures in August 1999, rose slightly to 107.77 yuan from 107.52 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 1.02 million lots from 1.06 million lots.
"Thin volume today indicates the contracts have little potential to post solid rises in the short term," a trader said.
